title: The Emu War
summary: Australia deployed soldiers with machine guns against roughly 20000 emus and effectively lost.

title: War of the Oaken Bucket
summary: Modena and Bologna went to war over a stolen wooden bucket; thousands died and Modena kept the bucket.

title: The Cadaver Synod
summary: Pope Stephen VI exhumed his predecessor's corpse and put it on trial in full papal vestments.

title: Great Molasses Flood
summary: A storage tank burst in Boston sending a wave of molasses through the streets at high speed.

title: Defenestrations of Prague
summary: Officials were thrown out of a castle window and survived by landing in a heap of manure.

title: War of Jenkins' Ear
summary: A war between Britain and Spain nominally triggered by a severed ear presented to Parliament.

title: The Dancing Plague of 1518
summary: Hundreds of people in Strasbourg danced uncontrollably for weeks and some reportedly died of exhaustion.

title: The Kettle War
summary: A conflict between Austria and the Dutch Republic in which the only casualty was a soup kettle.

title: The Pastry War
summary: France invaded Mexico partly over a French pastry chef's damaged shop and unpaid compensation claim.

title: Medieval animal trials
summary: European courts formally prosecuted animals including rats and pigs with defence lawyers appointed.

title: The Great Stork Derby
summary: A Toronto lawyer's will left his fortune to whichever woman bore the most children in ten years.

title: The Berners Street Hoax
summary: Theodore Hook won a bet by having thousands of tradesmen and dignitaries converge on one London address.

title: Tulip Mania
summary: Dutch speculators drove single tulip bulb prices above the cost of a house before the market collapsed.

title: The London Beer Flood
summary: A vat ruptured at a brewery releasing an enormous wave of porter into surrounding streets.

title: Operation Acoustic Kitty
summary: The CIA surgically implanted listening equipment in a cat to spy on Soviet officials.

title: The Bat Bomb
summary: The US developed a plan to attach incendiary devices to bats and release them over Japan.

title: Project Habakkuk
summary: Britain seriously pursued building an aircraft carrier out of reinforced ice.

title: The Tanganyika laughter epidemic
summary: A contagious outbreak of laughter closed schools and spread across villages for months.

title: Wojtek the soldier bear
summary: A bear was formally enlisted in the Polish army and carried ammunition at Monte Cassino.

title: The Great Chicago Fire cow myth
summary: A cow was blamed for starting a catastrophic fire on evidence a reporter later admitted inventing.

title: Isaac Newton and the South Sea Bubble
summary: The greatest scientific mind of the age lost a fortune speculating and said he could not calculate human madness.

title: The Pig War
summary: Britain and America came to the brink of war over the shooting of a single pig on San Juan Island.

title: Hannibal's vinegar rocks
summary: Ancient accounts claim Hannibal split Alpine boulders by heating them and dousing them in vinegar.

title: The Anglo-Zanzibar War
summary: The shortest war in recorded history lasted approximately 38 minutes.

title: Caligula's war on Neptune
summary: The emperor reportedly ordered his troops to attack the sea and collect seashells as spoils.

title: Poon Lim's survival raft
summary: A steward survived 133 days alone on a raft and the Royal Navy said it was a record he hoped no one would break.

title: Peter the Great's beard tax
summary: Peter the Great taxed beards and issued tokens proving the bearer had paid to keep his.

title: The Radium Craze
summary: Radioactive material was marketed in toothpaste water and suppositories as a health tonic.

title: Goat testicle transplants
summary: John Brinkley built a fortune implanting goat glands in men and nearly won a governorship.

title: The Cottingley Fairies
summary: Two girls fooled Arthur Conan Doyle with cardboard fairy cutouts photographed in a garden.

title: The Turk chess automaton
summary: A chess-playing machine astonished Europe for decades while concealing a human operator inside.

title: Phineas Gage's iron bar
summary: A railway worker survived an iron rod passing through his skull and walked away talking.

title: The Boston Molasses trial
summary: The subsequent court case ran for years and helped establish modern engineering liability standards.

title: Tycho Brahe's prosthetic nose
summary: The astronomer lost part of his nose in a duel over a mathematics disagreement and wore a metal replacement.

title: The Great Sparrow Campaign
summary: China ordered the extermination of sparrows which caused locust swarms and contributed to famine.

title: Cane toads in Australia
summary: Toads introduced to eat beetles ignored the beetles entirely and became a worse plague themselves.

title: The Halifax Gibbet and Yorkshire law
summary: Local custom permitted execution for theft above a set value leading to precise haggling over prices.

title: Nikola Tesla's pigeon
summary: The inventor declared he was genuinely in love with a specific white pigeon.

title: The Voynich Manuscript
summary: A book nobody has ever been able to read has consumed the careers of expert cryptographers.

title: The Diet of Worms
summary: A pivotal moment of the Reformation was held at an assembly whose name reliably amuses English speakers.

title: Lord Byron's pet bear
summary: Told he could not keep a dog at Cambridge Byron enrolled a tame bear instead as no rule forbade it.

title: The Molasses Act smuggling
summary: A tax so widely ignored that smuggling became the respectable default across the colonies.

title: Sweden's Vasa warship
summary: A magnificent warship sank about 1300 metres into its maiden voyage because it was too top-heavy.

title: The Tay Bridge disaster poem
summary: William McGonagall commemorated a tragedy in verse so bad it is still celebrated as the worst poetry ever written.

title: Pope Gregory and the missing days
summary: The calendar reform deleted ten days causing riots by people who believed their lives had been shortened.

title: The Astor Place Riot
summary: A deadly riot in New York was triggered by a dispute over which actor performed Shakespeare better.

title: The Straw Hat Riot
summary: New Yorkers rioted for days over the social rule that straw hats must not be worn after mid-September.

title: The Battle of Karansebes
summary: An Austrian army reportedly attacked itself in confusion after a dispute over alcohol.

title: Vlad and the Ottoman envoys
summary: Envoys who refused to remove their hats were reportedly given a permanent solution to the problem.

title: The Great Fire of London bakery
summary: A fire that destroyed most of the city began in a bakery on a street called Pudding Lane.

title: The Whisky Rebellion
summary: A tax on spirits provoked an armed uprising that a president personally rode out to suppress.

title: Emperor Norton of the United States
summary: A bankrupt San Francisco businessman declared himself Emperor and the city humoured him for decades.

title: The Cardiff Giant
summary: A fake stone giant fooled thousands and its rival fake outdrew the original.

title: Charles Waterton's practical jokes
summary: A naturalist greeted guests by biting their ankles from under the dinner table.

title: The Great Exhibition sparrow problem
summary: Sparrows infested the Crystal Palace and the solution proposed to the Queen was sparrowhawks.

title: Napoleon and the rabbits
summary: A rabbit hunt arranged for Napoleon went wrong when the tame rabbits charged the emperor instead.

title: The Ministry of Silly Postal Rules
summary: Before prepaid stamps recipients paid for letters leading to elaborate coded envelope scams.

title: Robert Liston's 300 percent mortality operation
summary: A famously fast surgeon reportedly killed the patient an assistant and a spectator in one procedure.

title: The Great Boston Fire horse flu
summary: An epidemic among horses paralysed transport and revealed how dependent cities were on animals.

title: Mary Toft's rabbit births
summary: A woman convinced prominent English doctors that she was giving birth to rabbits.

title: The Sausage Duel
summary: Rudolf Virchow reportedly proposed a duel with pork sausages one infected with parasites.

title: Kellogg and corn flakes
summary: Cereal was invented partly as an anti-stimulant intended to discourage certain private habits.

title: The Dreadnought Hoax
summary: Virginia Woolf and friends in disguise were given a state tour of a Royal Navy battleship.

title: The Man in the Iron Mask speculation
summary: A masked prisoner generated three centuries of increasingly elaborate theories about his identity.

title: Pope Formosus and the trial verdict
summary: The corpse on trial was found guilty and had its fingers removed before being thrown in the Tiber.

title: The Chevalier d'Eon
summary: A French diplomat and spy lived openly in two genders and London bookmakers took bets on the question.

title: Timothy Dexter's coals to Newcastle
summary: An eccentric merchant shipped absurd goods to absurd places by accident and got rich anyway.

title: The Bone Wars
summary: Two palaeontologists sabotaged each other so viciously they dynamited fossil sites out of spite.

title: Ignaz Semmelweis and handwashing
summary: A doctor who proved handwashing saved lives was ridiculed by colleagues and died in an asylum.

title: The Tsar's useless railway line
summary: Legend holds a ruler drew a railway route with a ruler including a detour around his own finger.

title: The Bermondsey Horse Meat panic
summary: Victorian food adulteration scandals involved chalk in bread and lead in sweets.

title: Lady Mary Montagu and inoculation
summary: Smallpox inoculation was promoted in Britain only after being tested on condemned prisoners.

title: The Ig Nobel Prize founding
summary: An annual prize honours research that makes people laugh and then think.

title: Pitch drop experiment
summary: An experiment so slow that the man watching it died before ever seeing a drop fall.

title: The Bald Knobbers
summary: A vigilante group in the Ozarks wore extremely alarming homemade horned masks.

title: Nicolas Chauvin and chauvinism
summary: A possibly fictional soldier's excessive patriotism gave the world a word still in daily use.

title: The Streetlight Riots of Pall Mall
summary: Early gas lighting terrified Londoners who feared the pipes would explode beneath their feet.

title: Boston's Great Brinks Robbery planning
summary: Robbers spent years rehearsing a heist and were caught days before the statute of limitations expired.

title: The Wright Brothers' patent war
summary: The inventors of flight spent their most productive years suing people instead of flying.

title: Charles VI the Glass King
summary: A French king suffered a delusion that he was made of glass and might shatter.

title: The Great Horse Manure Crisis
summary: Victorian cities predicted they would drown in manure and the problem solved itself entirely.

title: The Chinese Emperor's rain arrest
summary: Officials in some periods were formally punished for failures of weather.

title: The Erfurt Latrine Disaster
summary: A floor collapsed at a royal assembly dropping nobles into the cesspit below.

title: Alexander the Great's Gordian solution
summary: Faced with an unsolvable knot the answer chosen was simply to cut it with a sword.

title: The Roman fish sauce industry
summary: Romans built an empire-wide trade in a condiment made from fermented fish intestines.

title: The Speaker's dragging tradition
summary: New Speakers of the Commons are still ceremonially dragged to the chair reflecting a lethal job history.

title: Black Rod's slammed door
summary: Parliament ceremonially slams a door in the monarch's messenger's face every single year.

title: The Sausage Rebellion of Zurich
summary: The Reformation in Zurich was sparked partly by people defiantly eating sausages during Lent.

title: Trial by ordeal of the cursed morsel
summary: Accused clergy proved innocence by attempting to swallow dry bread without choking.

title: The Corpse Roads of England
summary: Medieval law required burial at specific churches creating long formal routes for carrying bodies.

title: Elizabethan sumptuary laws
summary: Laws dictated precisely who could wear which colours and fabrics by social rank.

title: The Window Tax
summary: A tax on windows led people to brick up their windows creating permanently dark houses.

title: The Hat Tax and its forgeries
summary: Britain taxed hats and criminals promptly began forging hat tax revenue stamps.

title: The Wig Powder Tax
summary: A tax on hair powder effectively killed the fashion for powdered wigs overnight.

title: The Brick Tax loophole
summary: Taxing bricks by number led builders to simply make enormous bricks.

title: Ship money and the constitutional crisis
summary: A tax for a navy on inland towns helped precipitate a civil war.

title: The Lord Mayor's coach and the Thames
summary: Ceremonial London processions were repeatedly disrupted by farcical logistical failures.

title: The Peasants' Revolt poll tax
summary: A deeply unpopular head tax triggered a national uprising and the burning of legal records.

title: The Rebecca Riots
summary: Welsh protesters dressed as women to destroy tollgates in an organised campaign.

title: The Swing Riots letters
summary: Agricultural protesters signed threatening letters with a fictional captain's name.

title: The Great Stink
summary: Parliament only funded London's sewers when the smell of the Thames became unbearable inside Westminster.

title: The Tichborne Claimant
summary: A butcher from Wagga Wagga convinced many that he was a missing English aristocrat.

title: Spring-heeled Jack panic
summary: Victorian London was gripped by reports of a leaping figure that no one could ever catch.

title: The Piltdown Man forgery
summary: A fake fossil fooled British science for forty years partly because it flattered national pride.

title: The Coal Hole and Judge and Jury Society
summary: Victorian Londoners staged mock trials as public entertainment in taverns.
